## Key facts [...] A total of 1.23 million people died from tuberculosis (TB) in 2024 (including 150 000 among people with HIV). Globally, TB is the world’s leading cause of death from a single infectious agent and among the top 10 causes of death.
 TB was also both the leading killer of people with HIV in 2024 and a major cause of deaths related to antimicrobial resistance. [...] In 2024, an estimated 10.7 million people fell ill with TB worldwide, including 5.8 million men, 3.7 million women and 1.2 million children. TB is present in all countries and age groups.
 Multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) remains a public health crisis and a health security threat. Only about 2 in 5 people with drug-resistant TB accessed treatment in 2024.
 Global efforts to combat TB have saved an estimated 83 million lives since the year 2000.
 TB is preventable and curable.
